catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 1b data and RMAT designation
detailed_catalyst_text: Phase 1b clinical data in severe hypertriglyceridemia were presented at AHA, showing mean Day 30 reductions of 65% in ANGPTL3 and 63% in triglycerides with favorable tolerability and no treatment-related serious adverse events. Reductions were maintained through at least 90 days, and the program also received RMAT designation for this indication, supporting potential expedited development.
catalyst_text_evidence: CRISPR Therapeutics today presented clinical data from its Phase 1b clinical trial evaluating CTX310®, an investigational, in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing therapy targeting angiopoietin-like protein 3 (ANGPTL3), in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG). A single-course treatment with CTX310 produced mean reductions from baseline at Day 30 of 65% in circulating ANGPTL3 and 63% in triglycerides (TG) in participants with a median baseline TG level above 1,000 mg/dL. These data were presented today during a late-breaking session at the AHA Scientific Sessions 2026 and build on the Phase 1a results, including one-year durability data presented at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Congress 2026 and published in The New England Journal of Medicine. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) recently granted Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designations to CTX310 for the treatment of sHTG and for the treatment of patients with elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C).

catalyst_text: Received RMAT designation for elevated LDL cholesterol
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA granted RMAT designation for the program in patients with elevated LDL cholesterol. This regulatory milestone can facilitate expedited development and review pathways for the therapy.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 1 idiopathic inflammatory myopathy data
detailed_catalyst_text: In the Phase 1 rheumatology basket, all nine idiopathic inflammatory myopathy patients achieved a moderate or major Total Improvement Score response. Consistent activity across IMNM, dermatomyositis, and antisynthetase syndrome supports potential broad efficacy in myositis.
catalyst_text_evidence: As of 2026-10-15, 21 patients have been dosed in the rheumatology basket: four in the SLE cohort, eight in the SSc cohort and nine in the IIM cohort. All nine patients with IIM, including two with immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM), two with dermatomyositis (DM) and five with antisynthetase syndrome (ASyS), achieved a moderate or major Total Improvement Score (TIS) response.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 1 systemic lupus data results
detailed_catalyst_text: In the lupus cohort, two of three evaluable patients maintained drug-free DORIS remission through at least nine months, with one beyond one year. These early results indicate durable disease control without ongoing immunosuppression.
catalyst_text_evidence: In SLE, two of three evaluable patients have maintained drug-free DORIS remission through at least Month 9, including one patient beyond one year.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 1 systemic sclerosis data
detailed_catalyst_text: Phase 1 systemic sclerosis data were presented showing 83% (5/6) rCRISS-25 responses at Month 3 among patients receiving standard lymphodepletion, with all responders maintaining response. These results, presented at a major rheumatology meeting, suggest meaningful early efficacy with a favorable tolerability profile.
catalyst_text_evidence: Data from the SSc cohort were presented in a poster session at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Convergence 2026. As of the data cut-off on 2026-07-21, seven patients with SSc dosed at the 100 million CAR+ cell dose level had at least three months of follow-up: At Month 3, 83% (5/6) of patients who received standard lymphodepletion achieved a revised Composite Response Index in Systemic Sclerosis (rCRISS)-25 response, including two patients who achieved the more stringent rCRISS-50 response. All five responders have maintained their response, including four patients who have completed at least six months of follow-up.
